• IUCN Red List: Least Concern (IUCN 2023)

This genus was previously placed in its own family, Ageneiosidae, and some publications still follow this arrangement.
South America: La Plata River basin: Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay. This species is widely distributed in the Paraná and Paraguay River basins.
Ageneiosus militaris lives in rivers, eating fish and microcrustaceans. In the Paraná River it is found in spring, summer and early fall.

They do not have parental care and fertilization is internal. In the breeding season males have ossified chins, modifications in the spine of the dorsal fin and the anterior anal fin rays form a gonopodium (Da Graça and Pavanelli, 2007).

Etymology: the genus name Ageneiosus means beardless, referring to the very small maxillary barbels. The specific name militaris means soldier or war-like, presumably referring to the long dorsal spine, serrated on both sides.
